The first part the PUT example in the documentation says to do a GET with "Content-Type" header instead of "Accept". This has been fixed in the bleeding edge page, but not the older pages.

Also in this example (and most), the docs show the returned resources in turtle (default), but the system returns `@prefix` and not `PREFIX`. Minor, but can be slightly confusing.  Not sure if it's worth changing.

And I'm not sure of proper protocol about changing these pages, so let me know if there is a process around this that I should have followed. Thanks!
Opening a ticket and then making changes is fine. Opening the ticket lets Andrew Woods know about the issue, editing the pages is a reasonable way to fix it. Good work!

For the PREFIX / @prefix thing, if the examples are using PREFIX and the rest of the example really is legit Turtle and the docs claim that the example is Turtle, sounds like just an ordinary typo. I'd fix it.
